title: Cells, ranges and the console
concept:
A spreadsheet is a grid. Every **cell** has an address: its column letter, then its row number. `G2` is column G, row 2. In the practice sheet that's the quantity of the first order, **{{=G2}}**.

The practice sheet is the order log of **Aegean Supplies**, an office-equipment distributor: 180 orders in columns A–H, and three small lookup tables to the right (products in J–N, sales reps in P–T, discount tiers in V–X).

A **range** is a rectangle of cells, written as its first cell, a colon, and its last cell. `G2:G181` means every cell from G2 down to G181: all 180 order quantities. `J2:N15` is a block five columns wide and fourteen rows tall: the product table.

Anything that starts with `=` is a **formula**. Excel works it out instead of showing what you typed. `=G2` shows whatever is in G2, and changes if G2 changes.

> [!tip] How practice works here: type a formula in the console (the `=` is optional), press Enter, and watch the sheet. Clay marks what a formula searched for, green where it matched, blue what came back. Drills are checked the moment you run them, and only formulas you type yourself count.

args.name: G2:G181
args.desc: a range: every cell in the rectangle between the two corners

worked.prompt: What is the total quantity of the first three orders?
worked.explain: `G2:G4` is the range of three quantity cells ({{=G2}}, {{=G3}} and {{=G4}}). SUM adds them: **{{=SUM(G2:G4)}}**. Run it and the three cells light up as the ones that were added.

mistakes: Writing the row first: `2G` isn't a cell. It's always column letter, then row number: `G2`.
A comma instead of a colon: `SUM(G2,G181)` adds just **two** cells; `SUM(G2:G181)` adds all 180.
Counting the header row: row 1 holds the column names, so the data starts on row 2.

drills.ask: What's the quantity of the first order? Point a formula at its cell (column G, row 2).
drills.hint: Quantity is column G and the first order is on row 2, so the cell is `G2`. Type `=G2`.

drills.ask: Return the product name in cell **K7**.
Add the quantities of the first two orders (G2 and G3) using `+`.
Total the quantities of the first five orders (G2 to G6) using a **range** inside SUM.
drills.hint: A range is first cell, colon, last cell: `G2:G6`. Put it inside `SUM( )`.

questions.prompt: Which cell is in column **H**, row **4**?
questions.explain: Column letter first, then row number: `H4`.

questions.prompt: How many cells are in the range `B2:C4`?
questions.explain: Two columns (B, C) × three rows (2, 3, 4) = 6 cells.

claimAfter: I can read cell addresses and ranges, and point a formula at them.
notYet: Locking references with `$` so formulas copy correctly, and functions beyond SUM. That's the next two lessons, then Level 1.
